title: Feeling That It Has Touched: A Torque Residual, a Threshold Above the Model's Error, and a Count of Ticks Before Believing It

questions.question: What is the residual?
options: The torque left when the arm has stopped
The torque measured less the torque the model says free motion needs
The filtered current of the motor
The difference between two joints' torques
questions.explanation: The model says what torque the motion should need. Whatever is measured beyond that is either the model's error or something pushing on the arm.

questions.question: A threshold of 0.05 N m gave how many false alarms with gravity 5 percent out?
options: 5, one for each percent
One every tick
questions.explanation: The model's own error was larger than 0.05 N m, so contact was declared before the wall. A threshold of 0.8 N m gave none.

questions.question: Which approach was a harder hit?
options: 0.2 rad/s, because it took longer to detect
Both the same, since the wall is the same
0.6 rad/s
Neither: both were detected before any torque built up
questions.explanation: At 0.6 rad/s the contact was found sooner, in 10 ms, but the arm was moving faster and the wall's torque reached 5.20 N m before it stopped.

questions.question: Why is the detection delayed?
options: The wall takes time to push back
The controller runs slower near a wall
The residual is filtered and has to stay over the threshold for a count
The joint's encoder lags the motor
questions.explanation: A filter smooths the residual and a count of ticks keeps one bad reading from being believed. Each adds a little delay.

questions.question: What does the count of ticks protect against?
options: One noisy tick being taken as contact
A model whose gravity term is wrong
A wall that is softer than expected
An approach that is too fast
questions.explanation: A model error is steady and is dealt with by the threshold. A single spike is over by the next tick, so it never reaches the count.

questions.question: What is not covered?
options: How fast the arm may approach
How large the threshold must be
How long detection takes
The force at the tip from all the joints
questions.explanation: This is one joint and its torque. Where on the arm the contact is, and with what force, needs every joint and the Jacobian.
